items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: he went back to Washington University and studied with a guy named Robert Wykes who was also a flautist

ctx.x: I know I have trouble, I’ve had trouble over the years trying to get my students to realize that they can’t just play what they want to if they want to work. You’ve got to be prepared for any situation, be able to take requests, and so it’s tricky. I’m going to guess that you learned what the word “gig” meant early on in life.

Real early on in life. I’ve got a ton of stories to tell you about gigs and Dad and all that kind of stuff. And I’ve probably seen more than most because I’ve seen great players scuffle to play this music. You know but he just sets it down there and you’ve just got to count this stuff off and go, and it doesn’t necessarily go all the time the way you actually want it to go. And then his career was really interesting too because he drove a streetcar in St. Louis for a while, but he always wanted to be into music…

That came to mind today because I was listening to some of his themes and you went from “The Six Million Dollar Man” with all these sirens and all this, and then to “The Virginian.” Like all of a sudden we’re going back like a hundred years and it’s sort of frontiery, and that’s just so admirable.
